beats: My kids read English words on their study wall, but they've never heard them spoken.
A word like suddenly was just letters — no clue how to say it, and IPA means nothing to a first-grader.
So I built a plain respelling dictionary — Norwegian letters instead of phonetic symbols. Suddenly becomes SAD-en-li.
It shows up under every vocabulary answer, beside each choice before they pick, and in their review history.
2,588 words. Every one of them now sounds like something.
